name: Idle Champions of the Forgotten Realms

pos.text: I've needed to stop playing this game for a long time.  Recent stability issues are kind of forcing me out now, app can only run a bit before disconnect and forced crash.  I want to give it a thumbs down for stability right now, but after 20k+ hours I think that would be petty haha.  I hope I don't pick this game up ever again, it's been real though.

This is my first "idler" but as someone who has always loved the roleplay side of DnD this is actually a super fun game. There's several "Campaigns" that are quite extensive with surprisingly good writing - some laugh out loud moments and some nice, moustache-twirling villains. The "fan service" includes characters from the broader world of DnD - books, games, tabletop roleplay, cartoons - and is both well researched and integrates well into a broader world of Faerun. 

If you are patient, you need to spend absolutely NOTHING to play this game effectively and well. The developers are incredibly generous with free giveaways and are concentrating hard on improving the experience for new players. Sure, the in-game shop has things to speed up your game or fun costumes, but not only are they all 100% optional you can earn them for free over time. Everyday the devs give you a small amount of f

I would rate this game as "guilty pleasure", since I load it up almost every day, to watch my group of heroes either struggle to survive or finally beat another wave of enemies - sometimes the game doesnt want you to win... Anyways, you can play this on multiple systems, and it works with any kind of controls.
Game has been enjoyable, and they've been dedicated to releasing new characters regularly since release in 2020. Great to see so many D&D greats in the game.

Best "idle" game out there. Honestly, it's not particularly idle. Monthly events, weekly challenges, all sorts of collectibles, very active Discord, multiple weekly streams, thousands of variants. Set up your team and go do something else...come back and you've either won or you need to adjust to hit your goal. Plenty of strategy, lots of ways to succeed. Always a new goal.

I've been playing this for a while now, and yes — it can get a bit predictable. But it’s definitely a long-haul type of game where unlocking achievements can take ages (I’m talking months, even years). If you’re prepared for a long grind, I’d definitely recommend it. It’s pretty low-key, though you’ll need to figure out the right character combinations for your party. Getting past levels like 400 or 600 can be a real pain, and it gets frustrating when certain stages limit the number or type of characters you can use — or when gear and unlock bonuses aren’t enough to push through.

Building up enough gems to get familiars can also be annoying, and sometimes even potions don’t give you the boost you need for tougher levels. That said, I like that the game keeps progressing and leveling up even when I’m not playing.

Fun and surprisingly deep game to learn at start thinking its just casual idle game, click and upgrade and win, but nah man this game hits different lets say there’s a lot to learn about characters and strategies, and while casual play covers only a small part, the game has a huge “iceberg” of content like gem farming and wall pushing. Complex at first, but simple once you get the hang of it.
Great afk game does get very repetitive and very grindy for new characters or gear

If you know, you know; if you don't; check it out.  Too much awesome to list.   Lots of stats to consider, Math, Formation/Balance, Nostalgia, Supportive and peaceful - all inclusive vibe, and so much more.   I would like to see MUCH less emphasis on monetary exchange but I enjoy supporting the game development and am confident that comparable results without such investment is realistic, although noticeably slower.   

Maybe I will have to play more just in case I am not clear on my humble perspective.

I stopped playing this game in 2023.

This is really fun for an idle game. It takes a broad approach to powering up, where gaining a greater quantity of heroes improves your combined power for more levels, and farming resources in the different "campaigns" improves your power overall in a flattened way.

Compared to other idle games this one bucks the trend of the transcension to instead add numerous campaigns with their own ascensions. And thr trascending gameloop is one akin to completing your deck & playing in the event-driven gamesystem.

It's very fun, and there's constantly new content to mentally engage with - most idle games instead become repetitive at this point - but the downside of this approach is the FOMO. Missing an event or halfassing it means you miss out on some power, and that motivation to play harder than you may want to causes you to burnout. 

Nevertheless, it's a
Kudos to the devs. Asked them to wipe my account so I can start over to relearn the game after years of not playing and they did it.

This game has it's good points. But it is notoriously buggy and the framerates at times can be abysmal. You can pop expensive consumables and then the server will go down negating your investments. It's fun from a F2P perspective, but spending money should be met with caution.
They added a smug barefoot smol fairy queen to the game. Game is now 1000% more worth it, my score: 1/5, thas my dong inches tall vs her inches tall

Free to play, but at minimum you need a few familiars to enjoy the game. You can farm a few of them for in-game currency and the rest will cost you money. If you are patient you can pick them up on sale. 

This game is a nearly never ending marathon. You do not need to be a whale to do hard content, but you need to be realistic as to what content to approach. For every mission you can't complete there can easily be 20-100+ you can.

Reading champion cards is absolutely vital. I currently have over 120 champions unlocked (haven't count recently) and can get at least 50 more. I read them frequently as I was away 3 years and many have changed. You will not be able to always use your best teams, so adaptation to mission conditions will be the difference in having steady progress and frustration.

This game requires a lot of thinking at times until you start amass power. Almost every action a

I have played D&D since 1978. Yeah, I'm old. But I still play and the memories of fantastic adventures keep me coming back through all editions.

That being said, WHO THOUGHT RESETING PROGRESSION WAS THE WAY TO GO?!?!?!?!?

D&D is about starting an adventure as a wide-eyed rookie. The sense of accomplishment that comes from leveling up and deciding how to develop your character is central to the game.

This not D&D, this is a PtW gacha that forces you to go through each adventure starting at 1st level and alone and not carrying your party over to the next adventure.

I like idlers, but this isn't D&D. If you're okay with that, it's a decent enough idler, just REALLY ticks me off about the one-shot nature of it. And then you start over. 

10 out of 100. This is NOT D&D. Uninstalled and removed from account.
Just finished the tutorial,  let's go.  It's fun so far.

For some reason I love idle games, and this is the one that has really grabbed me. They are constantly adding content and there is a lot to it (by the standards of idle games.)

It can be a little money hungry, but you can get by on free to play. If you like idle games and dnd, give I'd recommend it.

Not the most incredible game ever but I've been a fan of the forgotten realms since I was like 10 and I've read a lot of the books and played most of the games so it's fun to collect all the characters I've known for years :-) it's a little deeper in strategy than the usual idle game but there's not a ton of stuff to do so it's just a nice little way to waste some time

Slow steady progression and weekly deals allow for steady progress without spending money.  You get a little bit of premium currency once a day, and some skins and familiars are available in game from progression and standard in-game currency.  There are frequently event global unlocks, and there are codes collected on the internet for free chest stuff that ranges from character unlocks to in game chests or currency. 

One I established the above, I tossed the devs some cash of my own volition.  With like 4000 hours over several years, I think i've spent like $100 total, almost exclusively for charity support buys, or skins I liked.

Also, works great on Linux.

This is the best idle game i've ever tried.

I don't have any strong reason to definitely give it thumbs up or down really. Idler like there are many just you collect roster of heroes and is in DnD setting. Due to that you can somewhat familiarize yourself with pre-written adventure plots like Tomb of Annihilation. This is actually why I'm really sticking around - reading material. Even if events often redirect me from that. Many champions are also characters known from the community shows or skits so aside official setting you can get to know the fandom too!
I'd say it's a very non-invasive game so it's easy to keep flowing with it. I could speak of its mechanical nuances like figuring out the right formation or fine tuning your modron core but at the end of the day all optimizing will crash over "funnel more item level into hero". Can do F2P no problem but it will be a slow burn to push past your progression walls. So if you do c

Good semi-passive way to get your CRPG fix when you don't have the time or mental energy to commit to a real CRPG.  Main attraction for me is the Forgotten Realms IP, if it was just some new generic fantasy IP I probably would not have stuck with it.

I’ve been having a great time with Idle Champions of the Forgotten Realms. What really sets it apart for me is how well it ties into real D&D lore. It does not just feel like a generic idle game with fantasy paint on it — it genuinely feels connected to the Forgotten Realms and the larger Dungeons & Dragons universe.

Another huge plus is the inclusion of real-world characters from popular live-play streams. That adds a lot of personality and makes the roster feel special, especially if you already enjoy D&D shows and actual play content. Seeing those characters show up makes the game feel like a celebration of the broader D&D community.

The gameplay also has more depth than it first appears. A lot of the fun comes from making incremental gains by solving each formation puzzle. Figuring out how champions work together, adjusting your layout, and squeezing out better progress feels r

It's a top shelf idle game. It can be quite demanding if you want to do everything. Personally, I enjoy checking in a couple times a day and leaving it open to grind overnight. That's more than enough to get through the events which are the most important part of building a robust roster.

Formation building is fun and it's satisfying to come back to a variant you couldn't complete after collecting more champions.

[h1] Run, you fools! (с) Gandalf  
I'm serious, especially if you love getting 100% achievements.  
Your perfectionism will suffer, I guarantee it.   [/h1]
 [h2]Time will fly unnoticed, your electricity bills will skyrocket, because the game will play itself at night. By itself, yes. Because you can’t progress without it.  
Even the donations, which the game is basically built on, won’t give you a 100% success guarantee.  
Some friends on Steam will call you crazy and stop being your friends.  
You might start skipping lunches just to buy that precious pack with that champion who only fits one raid for one achievement. And after that, you’ll probably never use them again.  
And yes, if you don’t want to play it (attention!) all year round to not miss events where champions are given for free, you’ll be saving not just on lunches.   [/h2]
 [b]In terms of achievements, this game is basica
It's pretty fun! I can grind on other games on other consoles and keep managing my team... I love Minsc and Boo and the people from D&D Animated Series (You can actually have them on your team)...

neg.text:
I've been playing for years, and I have spent hundreds (if not thousands) of dollars on this, so please trust what I say:

Do not touch this game.

I'm not the kind that plays "free" games on any platform. I figured that I wasn't stupid enough to get into a "freemium" game, and certainly not enough to spend money. I don't play Clash of Clans, gatcha games, or any other mobile trash. I don't have mental issues, and I do not have an addictive personality. I'm just a normal person who liked D&D, and in 2017, I figured I'd give this a shot. How naive I was.

Just like any other modern phone game, this isn't intended to be a good game, and it isn't fun.
The goal is to addict you because that is how it's engineered from the start. And that's the entire point - it is a business model, not a game. That means it's packed with extremely predatory monetisation practices that nickel and dime you at

Having spent hundreds on the game packs+dlc and thousands of hours, I can say this is at best a 5/10 idle games.

The game start out well with a lot of things to work on and a lot of characters to collect especially if you want to build a dream team and focus entirely on that. The variants let you do a bit of thinking to figure out on what to do for that very stage instead of just using the same team the entire time to keep the game a bit more fresh.

However, as you play more and more of the game, the game crack will show and the crack is massive and cannot be ignored. The pace the game actually receives a meaningful update is even slower than other much smaller indie game that only work on their idle stuff more as a hobby. Instead of releasing new and better goals to work toward in general with more layers to the gameplay like most idle games do, this game instead focus on puking out n

Sadly, after all the time spent in this game (and some money to support them), it was time to quit. The game has changed from a fun idle game where you could set up a team and let it run through an adventure, to a babysitting game where you have to check the team every 2 minutes to modify it according to what happens during the adventure.
If you're looking for an idle incremental game, that's not what this one is anymore.

My time on idler cash grabs are over. I spent the greater part of a year leaving this program and my computer running to farm parties full of heroes to scale them and earn currency faster.

This game is a time sink, like most mobile gacha and monetized games are. Since the release of premium platinum currency, the cash grab has been even worse. With continually expiring/retiring bundles and such, each skin and feat and event having their own gated p2w style niche behind it, it's not a D&D experience.

This game became a chore, I started to see how I dreaded just mixing and matching my party to progress as one of the lower parts of sitting down at my computer to game, even though it likely took up 10-15 minutes tops. It also takes a good amount of CPU, even spiking sometimes.

Yes, with enough time and enough research, you can get into this game without spending any money. The game itself
The fact that the best Christmas codes were provided only for streamer audiance and expired fast, is a giant middle finger to all loyal players. Don't want to reward such behavior

This is an example of an idle game that commits one of the cardinal sins of idle games: it demands your attention.
A lot of your attention. An increasingly ungainly amount of your attention.
Yet I like many others tolerated it anyway. The game was charming, and undoubtably a step up over Codename Entertainment's previous game. 
Boiling frogs though we were, it became increasingly unpleasant and unsatisfying to play the game.
Do your patron weeklies every week, click all the upgrades this reset, complete the seasonal events (that run almost monthly), click all your upgrades again, reset and adjust your three parties that run at the same time, click all the upgrades for all three parties because the automation won't do that until you upgrade your modron cores to level umpteen, click all your upgrades again, gnash your teeth at the idea of clearing that one objective that will require you t

It's okay.  I remember when this game was free.  You enjoy it after awhile, but then a part of you is thinking.  For the price of a hero, you literally can buy a full blown game.  I have a lot of free to play games and it's not a constant purchase of heroes.  I like the nastalgia of D&D, but I'm not liking their microtransaction of what? $10 dollars for a hero.  Couldn't get a better pricing?  For the price of a bundle, we're now talking closer to triple AAA games.  After awhile the amusement wears off.

For the developers, you've successfully made work.

This game should come with a cubicle. After thousands of hours, I can safely say there is no joy here. Somehow even opening chests is work. Every week there's a lot you have to do, except the idle component takes out any actual gameplay and the fact that picking best specialisations isn't somehow automated or made easier, man even a simple button to simply max level every character as far as possible would make the work less and enjoyment more.

This game is purgatory.

I'm tired of them keep updating the game with nonsensical "challenges" just to get people to keep playing. Stop adding achivements, for the love of god, when they make no sense and just let us play the darn game.

Painfully slow to play, many systems designed to annoy you just enough to get you to pay to if not win certainly to play. 
Even if you decide to pay to support the game the prices are WILDLY overpriced for the value you get. There are over a hundred champions in the game which beyond the beginning you will find out you either have to pay to unlock them or use a time gate mechanic which requires 6 parts to unlock and you are locked into 1 part every three days and some luck 1% chance to loot it from a boss that appears every five levels. 
So that works out to a new champ (after about 40ish of them if you farm with Hank) to be a new champ every 18 days or so barring events where you can get more bang for your parts. 
It is called Idle Champions, but there is very little idle about it as you need to actively play until you can collect enough familiars and have a core sufficiently leveled up
Predatory and boring imo. No wonder people dont get far in this game based on the achivements. If you are gonna play it and know dnd its fun for a time but gets boring quite fast.

Done with this game. Done with the Agenda pushing crap. What it should have been was a celebration of characters throughout D&D's History. What it became was BS from these online people who played games D&D on a stream. Instead of adding more characters from the History of D&D stories, either Greyhawk or Forgotten Realms, you get characters out of nowhere emphasizing Non-Binary. I'm so sick of it and so over this crap. I kept quiet and played due to my love for classic characters, but no longer. I am so over this New Age crap. Never again will I spend a dime or give it anymore thoughts. Wizards of the Coast, Idle Champions of the Forgotten Realms, and any game or movie that keeps doing this is dead to me. I don't care who hates me or blocks me, but I am sick of it all. I'm so tired and angry of this crap. I'm done, I'm truly done supporting companies out of good faith.

I fell off this game years ago, I just couldn't keep up with it, I wanted to support it, but the new champions coming out every other week or so on rotation with events made it impossible to just focus on the Evergreen characters or the main campaign.  I eventually lost all interest trying to keep on top of that, and getting codes for unlocks via email, it was just, like how some people had mentioned, doing another job.

I've learned from one other game after this, that if a game doesn't respect your time and focuses almost entirely on FOMO, it's not worth your time (and especially your money), so play it for free until you get to a point that it no longer feels fun to play, and move on to the next game.

First of all,  IT IS FREE, so I guess try it?

If your time is valuable here are some thoughts:

Despite being an utterly brain-dead "idle" game it (like so many others) requires lots of clicking and managing while yet never really presenting a challenge.  There is no pause button which is very very annoying.  I did not enjoy myself.

I'd like to find an idle game where one can just chill, maybe watch a movie on the other monitor, pick out some goodies and level up choices now and then, maybe lose and have to rethink upgrade choices and puzzle it out... instead they all seem to require constant baby sitting.  I guess I'm the crazy one.

Cannot be played "Idle" despite the name. Difficulty creep over time isn't fun or engaging. Huge pain for 100% achievement hunters. Consistently has bugs and at times the core strategy for beating difficult missions is to use bugs/exploits. Not fun to play.
Progress is slow, they do everything to make it hard hoping they can milk you with their macrotransactions
P2W hell. Bad idler, requires constant upkeep to progress, adventures are short and if you get stuck you really have to restart.

Fun game at first, until you realize the progression is painfully slow unless you spend large sums of money to feel like you're making progress. In game purchases are too expensive, even on sale. I spent $30 on gems to get the D&D cartoon kids like Hank, Presto, Bobby etc, so i'm happy with that but I have no expectations of ever gearing them up because it's way too much $$$.

Flop: Even with all graphical features turned off, this relatively simple 2D idle game can become surprisingly resource-hungry and increasingly unstable. Over longer sessions, it seems to consume more and more resources and can eventually crash.

Top: The game has a huge cast of well-known Dungeons & Dragons characters, and because of that, it feels like a very complete and well-developed game.

There are, however, a lot of minor inconveniences and irritating design choices that add up over time.

It feels bloated. I am very aware that my PC is far from a gaming machine, but even so, a relatively simple 2D game with all the graphical extras disabled should run smoothly. The fact that it can become sluggish and resource-hungry feels excessive.
Too many things interrupt the gameplay. Some game mechanics require you to click directly on the game screen. If a window or notification ha

I'm by no means a completionist, but I am interested in achievements and hunting them, hoarding them, collecting them, whatever you want to call it.

With this game in particular, I kept coming back to reach 100% achievements over and over again, tens of times (for those achievement hunters who started playing this game when it first dropped, they might have even reached 100% *hundreds* of times by now).

Nevertheless, not even achievements were enough to get me to log back in at a certain point.

Is there fun to be had in this game? Yes
Is there strategy involved? Yes
Is it worth it? Hard to say.

I guess I would give this game a middle finger--I mean middle thumb, if I could. ^^ The good thing is that it finally helped me somehow stop caring about achievements, if only for a brief moment.. until I moved onto another game, where I suddenly started caring about them again :D

Back before I understood just how idle games worked, I thought I was having fun. But I was wrong. Don't let the 150 hours fool you. That's 150 hours of watching the game play itself. Actually, at some point you stop watching and you leave the game playing itself and you realize, about 150 hours in, you've wasted all of that time.

Save you money. Save you time. PLAY games. Don't watch them play themselves.
A positive review is not available in your region.
Money extraction machine with pay-to-win mechanics, you'll get oh so close to the goal line, but you can't quite get there without little boosts.

Combining strategy and idle is really neat in this game. Team building is fun. 

However, the progression without a guide is really rough. Most content feels convoluted, long-winded, or painfully contrived. Lucky for them, I'm an achievement junkie doing lines.

Honestly, it needs some design overhaul, as well as a re-focus on DnD vibes, with less of this gender-pseudo political garbage.
VERY HEAVILY PAY TO PLAY experience. idk how people play this successfully. ive got 300+ hours in and still feel very weak when i look up how others play or get through areas.
